newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to benefit from cash, not CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to benefit from cash, not CPI data.

text.p: Belgian bonds will probably ignore data on Tuesday showing domestic inflation is under control, but could benefit from coupon payments on more than 700 billion Belgian francs of outstanding paper, dealers said.
"The spread (over Bunds) could tighten a bit," one trader said, referring to the coupon payments on OLO 13 (7.00 pct, April 1999) and OLO 14 (7.25 pct, April 2004), which are both big bonds.
"I don't think investors will wait (for non-farm payrolls on Friday) before reinvesting," she added. Around 50 billion francs of coupons are due to be paid by the Treasury.

The preliminary Belgian consumer price index for April, due to be released by the economics ministry at around 1100 local (0900 GMT) on Tuesday is expected to show year-on-year inflation slowed to 1.37 percent from 1.46 percent in March, according to a Reuter poll of five analysts.

OLO traders did not expect the number, although showing little price pressure in the Belgian economy, to be supportive. "I don't think many people care," one dealer said, noting investors were more focused on U.S. data due to be released on Tuesday, including the U.S. employment cost index and durable goods orders.

OLO trade was thin on Monday as the market waited for Tuesday's U.S. data. The yield on the benchmark 10-year OLO maturing March 2007 BE286= was at 6.05 percent in late trade, up from 6.04 percent on Friday. The spread over equivalent Bunds edged out to 15 from 14 basis points.
